questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a pluggable, runtime-extensible policy system for high-signal services like API gateways, focusing on lifecycle, concurrency, and hot-reload.

## Key Concepts
- Strategy pattern for interchangeable policies
- Runtime registry for dynamic policy discovery
- Thread-safety and hot-reload considerations

## Code Example
```typescript
interface RequestContext { route: string; user: User; metadata: any }
interface PolicyDecision { allow: boolean; reason?: string; quotas?: any }
interface Policy { apply(ctx: RequestContext): PolicyDecision }
class PolicyFactory { create(config: any): Policy }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you version policies and rollback safely?
- How would you isolate policies across tenants and credentials?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime-extensible routing logic for streaming with low-latency and backpressure concerns. Requires a registry for pluggable policies, a clean, minimal interface, and non-blocking paths to sinks. Examines tradeoffs between hot vs cold storage and observability.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy pattern
- Registry and runtime extensibility
- Backpressure and non-blocking IO
- Hot-swapping configuration

## Code Example

```ts
interface Message { source: string; schema: string; ttl: number }
interface Sink { enqueue(msg: Message): Promise<void> }
interface RoutingPolicy { selectSink(msg: Message): Sink }
class PolicyRegistry { register(name: string, policy: RoutingPolicy): void; get(name: string): RoutingPolicy | undefined }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you test hot-swapped policies without risking data loss?
- How do you ensure observability across multiple sinks when routing fails?
